subject: Atlas Payments POC: success criteria & KPIs (latency, throughput, cost/token, quality) trial planning
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Sam Patel <sam.patel@atlaspayments.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 01 Jul 2029 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Atlas Payments POC: recap + proposed success criteria / next steps

Hi Sam — thanks again for the call earlier. Quick recap and a proposed plan so we can align on the POC success criteria and timeline. Please confirm or flag anything missing.

Summary of what we heard:
- Goal: Validate Redwood as production inference for transaction routing / customer support triage for Atlas Payments
- Key constraints: low-latency inference at scale, predictable unit cost, and high intent/answer accuracy for payment-related queries

Proposed POC scope (2-week trial):
1) Success criteria / KPIs (goal thresholds to pass POC)
   - Latency: P95 <= 150 ms for 1-2k token end-to-end generation (service-side; measured at our edge)
   - Throughput: sustained 200 requests/sec with 1.5x burst capability to 300 req/sec without SLA violation
   - Cost: token cost <= $0.0008 per token (including model + infra amortized per token) — we will provide cost modeling details in the eval plan
   - Quality: Intent classification accuracy >= 92% on your labeled eval set; hallucination/incorrect response rate < 1.5%

2) Evaluation plan
   - Redwood provides an eval harness + scripts (attached: redwood-eval-plan-v1.pdf) and a sample KPI sheet (mvp-kpi-sheet.xlsx)
   - Atlas to provide a representative dataset (50k sample requests + 2-3 crucial long-tail prompts) and baseline metrics (current latency/cost/accuracy)
   - Run throughput sweep + steady-state run for 24h to exercise caching/batching behavior

3) Timeline & ownership
   - Kickoff: Jul 8 (Mon) — infra/kickoff call (30 min)
   - Redwood owners: Jordan (commercial lead), Marissa (engineering lead)
   - Atlas owners: Sam (product/PO), Nina (performance/security lead)

4) Deliverables
   - Redwood: eval harness, recommended model/quantization profiles, per-route latency/cost report, and a short results deck
   - Atlas: dataset + baseline metrics, access to test environment or synthetic request generator

Next steps
- Please confirm dataset delivery date and whether we can access any synthetic load generator (or if Atlas wants us to simulate traffic)
- Confirm kickoff time on Jul 8; I’ll send a calendar invite once we lock time.

Attachment: redwood-eval-plan-v1.pdf (application/pdf, 420KB)
Attachment: mvp-kpi-sheet.xlsx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet, 45KB)

Thanks,
Jordan Blake
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
jordan.blake@redwood.com
From: Sam Patel <sam.patel@atlaspayments.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 02 Jul 2029 09:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Atlas Payments POC: recap + proposed success criteria / next steps

Jordan — thanks for the clear recap. This looks reasonable and close to what we discussed. A few clarifications from our side: 

1) Cost/token: can you confirm whether that $0.0008 is just model inference compute or includes bandwidth / egress / Redwood platform overhead? We’ll need the breakdown for procurement.

2) Baseline metrics: we can share our baseline CSV with P50/P95 latency and current throughput numbers. Expect to have that to you by Thu (Jul 4). Is that timing OK?

3) For quality: our dataset includes labeled intent and a small set of annotated edge cases. We’ll include an initial 5,000 labeled subset for quick validation and the full 50k by the first week of the POC.

Also looping in Nina (cc’d) from performance/security for any network or compliance constraints.

We’re happy to kick on Jul 8 — propose 10:00am PT.

Regards,
Sam Patel
VP Product — Atlas Payments
Sam.Patel@atlaspayments.com
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 03 Jul 2029 11:25:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Atlas Payments POC: infra plan + test harness

Quick engineering note on what we’ll run and what we need from Atlas:

Plan:
- Stand up a dedicated POC route on Redwood Dedicated with isolated pool to reproduce realistic contention and to measure tail latency.
- Test harness will run the following: warmup (1h), steady-state ramp to target throughput (200 rps), 24h steady run, stress bursts to 300 rps for 30 min.
- Measurements: P50/P95/P99 latency, token throughput, model-side GPU utilization, batching stats, and observed cost per token from runtime counters.

What we need from Atlas:
- Dataset upload location + sample generator (or schema)
- Any IP ranges we should allow from your test environment (if you want to hit our test endpoint directly)
- Security contacts and any minimal checklist for data handling during the POC

I’ll upload the harness scripts and a quick runbook to the shared drive: https://drive.redwood.internal/drive/atlas-poc/eval-plan

-Marissa
Sr. Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Nina Gomez <nina.gomez@atlaspayments.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>, Sam Patel <sam.patel@atlaspayments.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 05 Jul 2029 16:40:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Atlas Payments POC: recap + proposed success criteria / next steps

Thanks Jordan/Sam — quick notes from performance/security: 

- Timeline: Jul 8 kickoff works for our side. We’ll join the run-level checks on day 1 and the 24h steady-state run.
- Metrics: would prefer a slightly tighter P95 latency threshold for top-tier flows (authorization-related prompts) — P95 <= 120ms for those routes. Can Redwood surface per-route P95 in the reporting?
- Baseline: attaching a small baseline export (atlas-baseline.csv) with our current P50/P95 numbers and sample QPS.

Attachment: atlas-baseline.csv (text/csv, 18KB)

Also a question on data handling: during the POC, we’ll only share anonymized samples. Please confirm Redwood will not persist raw inputs beyond the POC and that logs are access-controlled — we can sign an NDA addendum if needed.

Best,
Nina Gomez
Director, Performance & Security — Atlas Payments
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Sam Patel <sam.patel@atlaspayments.com>, Nina Gomez <nina.gomez@atlaspayments.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 07 Jul 2029 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Atlas Payments POC: recap + proposed success criteria / next steps

Perfect — thanks for the quick responses and the baseline, Nina. To confirm next steps and owners before kickoff: 

1) Confirmed kickoff: Mon Jul 8, 10:00am PT (invite sent): https://cal.com/redwood/atlas-poc-kickoff
2) Dataset delivery: Atlas to provide 5k labeled subset by Jul 4 (Sam) and full 50k by Jul 12 (Sam)
3) Per-route latency ask: we’ll include per-route P95 in the report. For authorization flows we’ll aim for P95 <= 120ms and we’ll flag any deviations in the daily report
4) Cost breakouts: Marissa will publish a cost breakdown (model compute vs infra vs platform) in the eval report so procurement has numbers for the $/token line item
5) Security: Jordan to connect Nina with our security lead for the short POC checklist and the data handling NDA addendum

Action items (owners):
- Sam (Atlas): deliver dataset + baseline, share network/IP constraints (by Jul 4)
- Marissa (Redwood): upload harness + runbook to shared drive, publish cost breakdown (by Jul 9)
- Jordan (Redwood): send kickoff invite + schedule 30-min results review at end of trial (target Jul 22)

We’ll track these in a shared doc and I’ll post interim status after the first 24h steady run. Looking forward to getting started.

Attachment: redwood-eval-plan-v1.pdf

Best,
Jordan Blake
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
